scope: Bounded local model two-pass single-card review; not independent human approval.

cards.title: The Third Detail Matters
cards.instruction: Choose one arbitrary detail and treat it as the key that explains, controls, or prevents the entire impossible situation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Keep that pebble level. It's the only thing holding Tuesday here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It's an ordinary pebble.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly why Tuesday trusts it.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Can I put it down?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: On a level surface. Wednesday's waiting for a mistake.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our ferry's floating above the harbour. Keep that souvenir pebble level; it's the only thing stopping us tipping.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I picked it up for you. I need my hands for the bags.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put it in my lunchbox. I'll keep the ferry level.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your sandwiches make it tilt.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll flatten them into a level bed. Lunch can suffer; the passengers mustn't slide off.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 makes a pebble's level position responsible for holding Tuesday; A3 uses its ordinariness as supporting evidence.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 directly absorbs B2's ordinary-pebble objection; B4's request to put it down determines A5's level-surface condition.

relationship.evidence: B4 wants relief from holding the pebble, and A5 offers a constrained way to achieve it.

heightening.evidence: A5 makes the proposed handover carry the risk of Wednesday exploiting a mistake.

specificity.evidence: A1 gives B a small object and an immediate holding requirement, though the surrounding location remains open.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's explanation of Tuesday's trust economically reinforces the arbitrary detail instead of introducing another object.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 makes an arbitrary souvenir pebble the sole safeguard against the airborne ferry tipping. A3 and A5 consistently organize action around keeping that detail level.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 needs free hands for bags, so A3 proposes transferring the pebble to A's lunchbox. B4 identifies the sandwiches as the source of tilt, so A5 proposes flattening them.

relationship.evidence: B2 reveals that the pebble was a gift for A and asserts a practical luggage need. B4 tests A3's proposed solution, making B a participant with useful objections.

heightening.evidence: A5 sacrifices lunch and specifies the danger to passengers after B4's sandwich objection. This develops the game, but the ferry-wide stakes were already established in A1.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a floating ferry and a level pebble; B2 and A3 supply bags and a lunchbox. The opening states the fantastic premise somewhat directly, but the physical task is clear.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's lunchbox solution is concise and usable. A5's willingness to flatten lunch earns its comic disproportion through B4, although the passenger explanation slightly underlines the joke.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2's need to carry bags prompts A3 to take responsibility for supporting the pebble in a lunchbox.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 reveals that the lunchbox contents undermine level support. A5 changes those contents by proposing to flatten the sandwiches.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: A1 assigns the ferry's stability to one arbitrary pebble; A3 and A5 sincerely solve ordinary handling problems as matters of passenger safety.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 increases A's personal commitment by sacrificing lunch to the pebble's supposed control of the ferry, although the overall stakes increase only slightly.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A assigns an arbitrary small detail decisive control over an entire impossible situation and organizes practical choices around preserving it.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: General magical superstition can accumulate charms; this card commits to one chosen detail as the controlling key.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: A1 assigns the airborne ferry's stability to a souvenir pebble's levelness; A3 changes its container and A5 flattens lunch while preserving that single arbitrary condition.

records.recommendedEdit: Kept the ferry trip, gifted pebble and lunchbox workaround, but replaced the ungrounded Tuesday claim with an explicitly airborne ferry in A1. This is a new illustrative impossibility, not a change to the card. Separate internal reread: fidelity 5, A1/A3/A5 make the same incidental pebble orientation control the whole vessel; logic 5, B2's bags cause A3's container offer and B4's sandwich tilt causes A5's flattening; relationship 4, B2 needs free hands and A takes the burden; heightening 4, A5 sacrifices lunch to protect all passengers; specificity 4, A1 establishes the harbour and impossible ferry before naming the detail; wit 4, A5 makes sandwich preparation carry responsibility for everyone aboard. Total 90. Five spoken ABABA turns, under 75 words; internal review only.
records.remainingConcern: Heightening is modest: A5 mainly repairs the previous solution. The concrete sacrifice and uninterrupted causal chain support acceptance without a rewrite.
records.writerReservation: The airborne ferry is established in dialogue, but the pebble's supposed control remains A's unsupported attribution. The final practical compromise leaves the difficulty of keeping a lunchbox level unresolved and playable.
records.alternativeComparison: The preserved kettle alternative protects a scratch while negotiating B's desire for tea. This candidate accepts responsibility for a gift and adapts a cooperative solution to B's luggage needs; its tactic is accommodating rather than initially prohibitive.

cards.title: The Third Detail Matters
cards.instruction: Choose one arbitrary detail and treat it as the key that explains, controls, or prevents the entire impossible situation.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't press the third button on the kettle. That's the moon's dimmer.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: How do we make tea?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use the first two. Tea and lunar stability are separate jobs.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The third one's flashing.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then the moon wants attention. Don't reward it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Don't press the kettle's third button. That tiny scratch on it is keeping the moon lit.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's the boil button. I want tea.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Use a saucepan. We can't risk smoothing the scratch.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll press it with my fingernail, around the scratch.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let me guide your hand. Everyone reading by moonlight is relying on this cup.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 selects the third kettle button as the moon's dimmer, though this can read as an actual magical control rather than A's arbitrary attribution.

responseLogic.evidence: A3 offers B2 a tea method; A5 interprets B4's flashing button, but changes from dimming to attention-seeking.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants tea, and B4 reports a device change that complicates A's proposed separation of functions.

heightening.evidence: A5 advises ignoring the flash without increasing the cost or commitment of protecting lunar stability.

specificity.evidence: A1 establishes a kettle with numbered buttons and an immediate prohibition.

brevityWit.evidence: A3's separate jobs for tea and lunar stability is concise, while A5 introduces a looser parenting joke.

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 singles out a tiny scratch as sustaining moonlight; A3 protects it and A5 supervises its preservation during use.

responseLogic.evidence: B2's tea need prompts A3's saucepan alternative; B4's fingernail workaround prompts A5's guided-hand compromise.

relationship.evidence: B2 wants ordinary tea and B4 bargains with a method that accommodates A's scratch theory.

heightening.evidence: A5 accepts B4's risky method while taking personal control and extending responsibility to everyone reading by moonlight.

specificity.evidence: A1 locates the scratch on a kettle button; B2 and B4 give actors concrete tea-making and fingernail actions to discuss.

brevityWit.evidence: A5's reliance of moonlight readers on 'this cup' earns its scale contrast from the negotiated button press.

hardGateEvidence.b2CausesA3: B2 identifies the necessary boil button and wants tea; A3 offers a saucepan to preserve the scratch.
hardGateEvidence.b4CausesA5: B4 proposes pressing around the scratch; A5 agrees to guide the hand through that precise operation.
hardGateEvidence.cardContribution: The scratch remains the sole arbitrary detail governing A's understanding and choices.
hardGateEvidence.sameGameHeightened: A5 turns prohibition into personally supervised participation with worldwide stakes.

mechanismDistinction.mechanism: A treats one arbitrary physical detail as the key to sustaining an impossible cosmic condition.
mechanismDistinction.confusableConcept: Operating an established magical device follows known controls; this card elevates an incidental detail into the decisive cause.
mechanismDistinction.distinguishingEvidenceRequired: Revised A1 locates lunar stability in a tiny scratch, and A3 and A5 protect that same scratch through B's tea-making proposals.

records.recommendedEdit: Retained the kettle's third button and lunar stakes, adding an incidental scratch. Internal reread: fidelity 5, logic 5, relationship 4, heightening 4, specificity 5, wit 4 = 92. B2's need produces A3's saucepan alternative; B4 proposes avoiding the scratch, causing A5 to guide the hand and assume responsibility for moonlit readers.
records.remainingConcern: No rewrite needed. A1's kettle with a third button is slightly unusual but immediately understandable.
records.writerReservation: The new scratch is now the decisive detail, so provenance cannot silently describe the button itself as the sole controlling object.
records.alternativeComparison: Alternative b uses bargaining and a shared precision task; a grants conditional release from holding a pebble.
